settings.label: Healthy Skin Barrier Lipid Ratio
settings.note: When this ratio is disrupted, moisture escapes and irritants enter. Replenishing ceramides directly restores the balance.

settings.title: Your barrier isn't broken. It's just depleted.
settings.body:
Your skin barrier is a lipid lattice: ceramides, cholesterol, and fatty acids in a ratio of roughly 50:25:25. Over-exfoliation, harsh cleansers, Pakistan's hard water, and even stress strip this mortar layer by layer.

The result? Skin that feels tight, reacts to everything, and can't hold moisture. You put on moisturiser and it feels like it evaporates within the hour. Fragrance that never bothered you starts stinging. Actives that used to work now cause irritation. That's not sensitivity — that's a barrier that needs rebuilding.

The fix isn't more products — it's replacing what was lost. Ceramides replace the lipids directly. Niacinamide stimulates your skin to produce more of its own ceramides. And that combination — external reinforcement plus internal stimulation — is how you actually repair a compromised barrier, not just mask the symptoms.

settings.text: Moisturiser seems to evaporate within an hour

settings.name: Ceramides
settings.desc: Directly replaces the lipids stripped by cleansers, hard water, and exfoliants. Fills the gaps in your barrier immediately.

settings.name: Niacinamide
settings.desc: Signals your skin to produce its own ceramides. External repair and internal stimulation simultaneously.

settings.name: Hyaluronic Acid
settings.desc: Draws and holds moisture once the barrier is intact enough to keep it there. Works better when ceramides are in place.

settings.name: Panthenol
settings.desc: Pro-vitamin B5. Calms inflammation and supports the skin's own healing process. Useful during recovery phase.

settings.tagline: Ceramides that repair. Niacinamide that rebuilds. Hyaluronic Acid that holds.

settings.note_html: The niacinamide in the serum also builds your barrier — it reinforces ceramide production and reduces trans-epidermal water loss. So when you use both, you're getting barrier support from two products simultaneously. The serum doesn't replace the moisturizer. But it does make the whole stack more effective.
